summary: The delta e705f22..7c72263 (c:\Users\Akash\Desktop\Projects\.openforge\work\F-20261119-12\review-delta.diff) only touches 3 test files under services/user-service/user-service-app/src/test/java/com/acme/ecommerce/user/outbox/. It has no changes to production code, config, migrations, dependencies or secrets. OutboxMigrationIT gets stronger. The old check upper-cased the SQL and used a Java string literal with a bare \b, which compiles to a backspace character, so the guard could never match anything. The new check is a precompiled case-insensitive DESTRUCTIVE pattern on the raw SQL with real word boundaries, plus a new test (guardPatternBites) proving the pattern catches DROP and ALTER and ignores identifiers like 'altered_things'. UserOutboxRelayIT gets stronger too: it now asserts that last_error on a DEAD row is exactly 'java.lang.IllegalStateException: Corrupt outbox payload'. That string is a fixed exception message with no payload or PII in it. UserDeletionOutboxIT.cancelledDuringBlockerCheckIsNotErased drops one assertion, that runDue returns zero. The checks that matter for security are still there: the request stays CANCELLED, the profile email stays un-anonymised (count of 'del-%' remains 1), the address is not deleted, and no outbox row is written. So the protection against erasing a cancelled request is not weakened. The test now has the same shape as cancelLeavesNothing. No security assertion was weakened, and there are no blocker, major or minor findings.
